verses.1: He reigned for seven years as king. He ruled in Jerusalem for forty years. His mother’s name was Zibya from Beer Sheva.
verses.2: And Yoash did what was right in the eyes of Jehovah, every day. The priest knew this.
verses.3: And Yehoyadav married two women, and he had sons and daughters.
verses.4: And after that, he had a sad heart and decided to rebuild the house of Jehovah.
verses.5: And he summoned the priests and the Levites, and said to them, “Go into the cities of Judah and gather together all the silver from Israel, so that you may strengthen the house of God over time. Come quickly about this task, and do not delay.”
verses.6: And the king called for Yehoyada, the chief priest. He said to him, “Yehoyada, do not ask for any payment from the people. Instead, bring back from Judah and Jerusalem the remains of Moses, the servant of God. Also, bring back the people of Israel to the Tabernacle.”
verses.7: For the wicked Tamar’s children broke into the house of God. And all the sacred objects in the house of Jehovah became property of those people.
verses.8: And the king said, “Let us build a altar. Then we shall offer sacrifices at the gate of the Temple of Jehovah.”
verses.9: And they sent out messages in Judah and Jerusalem, asking that Moses’ servant, the servant of God, be brought back to Israel in the wilderness.
verses.10: And all the singers and all the people were happy. They brought them out and threw them into the fire.
verses.11: And it happened that when he brought the treasure to the king’s palace, carried by the Levites. They saw that the treasure was very valuable. Then the king’s scribe and the chief priest came and examined the treasure. They then carried it away and placed it back in its proper place. This is what they did every day. In those days, they collected a great deal of money.
verses.12: And the king gave them to those who were responsible for carrying out the work in the house of God. They became laborers and workers, helping to build the house of God. They also worked as blacksmiths and metalworkers, in order to strengthen the house of God.
verses.13: And the workers did their work. They built the house of God on its proper foundation. Then they set up the house of God on its proper place.
verses.14: And they brought them before the king. Then He knew about the rest of the money, and he used it to make utensils for the house of God—vessels for worship, tables, chairs, and all kinds of gold and silver items. These were always kept in the house of God, throughout all the days of Jehoiada.
verses.15: And Yehoyada grew old, and he lived for many years. He died at the age of one hundred and thirty years.
verses.16: And he was buried in the city of David, along with the kings, because he did good deeds in Israel and with God. And in his house.
verses.17: And after his death, the leaders of Judah came and bowed down to the king. Then the king heard from them.
verses.18: They abandoned the house of Jehovah, their God. They worshiped the idols and other false gods instead. As a result, punishment was inflicted upon the Jews and Jerusalem because of their actions.
verses.19: And he sent angels to bring them back to Jehovah. But they testified against them, and they were not listened to.
verses.20: And the Spirit of God remembered Zaccharias, son of Jehovah. The priest stood before the people and said to them, “What are you doing? You are breaking the commands of Jehovah. You will not succeed, for you have abandoned Jehovah and left Him.”
verses.21: And they set up a wooden cross over him, in accordance with the king’s command, in the courtyard of the house of Jehovah.
verses.22: And Joash, the king, did not remember the kindness that his father Jehoiada had done to him. He killed his own son. And as for his burial, Jehovah said, “Let it be buried in a proper manner.”
verses.23: And during that year, the army of Amalek attacked. They came to Judah and Jerusalem. They destroyed all the leaders of the people, as well as all their possessions. They sent these people to King Darius.
verses.24: For in times of sorrow, people came to worship the idols of Aram. But God gave them countless enemies, because they abandoned Jehovah, their God, and made false judgments.
verses.25: And when they left him, it seemed as though they had abandoned him in great suffering. His servants rushed to help him, but the priest killed him on his knees. He died, and he was buried in the city of David. He wasn’t buried in the tombs of kings.
verses.26: And these are those who are connected to him: Zavad son of Shemaath the Ammonite, and Yehozavad son of Shimerit the Moabite.
verses.27: And his sons became too many for him to manage them. The laws of God are written down in the Book of Kings. Amasya was his son, who ruled under him.
